chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Ibrahim ibn Mahziyar from Ali ibn Mahziyar who said:

I asked him about the person in ihram who has meat from the game of hunting in his provisions: is it permissible for him to keep it with him without eating it, and bring it into Mecca while he is in ihram, so that when he exits ihram he eats it? He said: 'Yes, if it was not his own hunt.'
And there is no harm if the person in ihram buys a camel in the Haram (sanctuary) and takes it with him wherever he wishes. It was narrated.

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (specifically the Haram of Mecca)
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.صَادَهُ: His own hunt (as opposed to another's)

ai.seo_question: Can a pilgrim in ihram carry hunted meat in their provisions without eating it until they exit ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between consuming hunted game and merely possessing it, ruling that a pilgrim may carry meat from a non-pilgrim's hunt without incurring penalty, provided they do not eat it while in the state of *ihram*. It further extends this permissibility to purchasing a camel within the sacred precincts (*Haram*) to transport out, highlighting the flexibility in handling provisions during pilgrimage. This ruling is situated within the broader chapter on expiation (*Kaffarah*) for unintentional violations of *ihram* conditions.
